headline: IER adds gradient-estimation reliability to sparse on-policy distillation
summary: The paper analyzes sampled-token on-policy distillation (OPD) and defines an information-efficiency ratio (IER) for the reliability of reverse-KL gradient estimates at a fixed prefix. It approximates IER on a finite top-K candidate set and combines the resulting token ranking with existing usefulness scores. Across selected mathematical and medical reasoning settings, the authors report that combined selectors can approach or exceed full OPD at 0.1%–1% token budgets, with mixed results across settings. This concerns token selection for the loss: full student responses and teacher supervision remain computed, and proportional end-to-end compute savings are not established.
